Raise the site version and print the release commands

Source: R/release-supplement.R
release_supplement.Rd

release_supplement() prepares a release of a site. It runs check_supplement() and stops when that finds a problem, or when one of the files that it writes changes while the check runs. It then raises version in _supplement.yml, writes CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json again with the new version, and prints the git and GitHub commands that make the release. It runs none of these commands, so you can read them first and run them yourself in the site folder.

Usage

release_supplement(bump, path = ".")

Arguments

bump

"patch", "minor", "major", or a version such as "1.0.0".

path

The folder of the site.

Value

The release commands as a character vector, invisibly.

Details

bump is one of:

  • "patch", "minor", or "major": raise that part of the version by 1 and set the parts after it to 0. "minor" makes 1.9.3 into 1.10.0. An empty version counts as 0.0.0, so "major" gives a first release 1.0.0.

  • A version such as "1.0.0": three whole numbers joined by ., each 0 or without a leading zero. It must be greater than the current version, compared part by part as numbers, so 1.10.0 is greater than 1.9.0.

The function stops, and changes no file, when check_supplement() finds a problem or skips its git checks. It runs the check without web_links and renv_lock, so it requests no web address and does not compare renv.lock with the stored output: it gives neither the "renv-mismatch" nor the "renv-missing" row. A "doi-mismatch" problem for CITATION.cff does not stop it, because the release writes that file again. A change to _supplement.yml, CITATION.cff, or .zenodo.json during the check also stops it, as described below.

Only the value on the version: line of _supplement.yml changes, so its comments and the rest of its text stay as they are. The new value is written in double quotes. The line must be a one-line version: value directly under supplement:, as in the template. When it is missing, add version: "" under supplement: by hand.

The function reads _supplement.yml, CITATION.cff, and .zenodo.json before it runs check_supplement(), and reads them again after the check. When the bytes of one of these files changed while the check ran, or one of them was made or removed as a file, for example because you saved _supplement.yml, the function stops and writes none of the three files, so you can run it again. A change saved after the function reads the files again, until it finishes, can still be lost.

Before it runs check_supplement(), the function makes the new text of CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json from _supplement.yml with the new version. So a value that write_citation() or write_zenodo() refuses, such as an empty citation, stops the function with the class and message of that function's error, before the check runs and before any file is changed.

Before it changes any file, the function stops when CITATION.cff or .zenodo.json is a link, because a write would go through the link, or is a folder, or is a file that it cannot read or write. It also stops when one of them does not exist and its folder cannot be written. It looks for these when it reads the two files, before and after the check. If writing _supplement.yml, CITATION.cff, or .zenodo.json stops, for example when the disk is full, or is interrupted, the function puts back the old text of each of these files that changed, removes each one that it made, and stops. It prints the commands only after the three files are written, so an error or an interrupt while it prints keeps the files of the release.

The printed commands, for version X.Y.Z, are git status -- ., git add -A -- ., git commit -m "Release vX.Y.Z" -- ., git tag vX.Y.Z, git push, git push origin vX.Y.Z, and gh release create vX.Y.Z --generate-notes. The -- . limits the first three commands to the site folder: git status shows, and git add and git commit stage and commit, only files under the site folder. These are the files that the "large-file" and "saved-object" checks of check_supplement() read, so docs/, _freeze/, and figures/ reach the release when git does not ignore them, as in the template. When the site is a subfolder of its repository, a change outside the site folder, also one that was staged before, stays out of the release commit. A file outside the site folder that was staged before the release stays staged, so a later git commit adds it. The last command needs the GitHub command-line tool (gh). When Zenodo's GitHub integration is turned on for the repository, Zenodo archives the release and gives it a version DOI. Add that DOI to zenodo.version-doi in _supplement.yml, and render the site again, so that the home page shows it.

Errors

An error while the function prints the commands, after it wrote the files, reaches you as it is. Otherwise the function stops with an error of class supplement_error and one of these classes. When it stops with one of these classes, no file is changed, unless a file that changed cannot be put back. The supplement_error_release_write message then names that file.

The function checks in this order, and stops at the first problem: bump and path; _supplement.yml (no file, not UTF-8, not valid YAML, no supplement map); the current version and bump; the version: line; the values that the new CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json hold; the two output files; check_supplement(); an output file that is now a link, a folder, or a file that cannot be read or written, also when another file changed; a file that changed during the check; the problems that check_supplement() found; the writes.

  • supplement_error_argument: bump is not one of the forms above, or path is not a single non-empty string.

  • supplement_error_no_metadata, supplement_error_no_map: as for write_citation().

  • supplement_error_encoding: _supplement.yml is not UTF-8 text.

  • supplement_error_parse: the yaml package cannot read _supplement.yml, as for write_citation().

  • The classes that write_citation() lists for a value in _supplement.yml, such as supplement_error_missing_field, supplement_error_license, supplement_error_orcid, and supplement_error_author_name: a value that write_citation() or write_zenodo() refuses. The error has the same class and message as theirs, names release_supplement(), and comes before check_supplement() runs.

  • supplement_error_field_type: version is a list, or YAML reads it as a number or as true/false, such as an unquoted 1.10. Write it as one value in quotes, such as "1.10.0". Another value of the kinds that write_citation() names also gives this class.

  • supplement_error_doi: a DOI in _supplement.yml is not a DOI, as for write_citation().

  • supplement_error_version: version is not empty and is not a version, or the version in bump is not greater than it.

  • supplement_error_no_version: _supplement.yml has no one-line version: value directly under supplement:.

  • supplement_error_yaml: the yaml package does not read the changed _supplement.yml as the old file with the new version.

  • supplement_error_changed: _supplement.yml, CITATION.cff, or .zenodo.json changed while check_supplement() ran. This error comes before a supplement_error_release_check error. When CITATION.cff or .zenodo.json is now a link, a folder, or a file that cannot be read or written, the supplement_error_file_exists or supplement_error_write error comes instead, also when another file changed.

  • supplement_error_release_check: check_supplement() found a problem other than a "doi-mismatch" problem for CITATION.cff, or it skipped its git checks.

  • supplement_error_file_exists: CITATION.cff or .zenodo.json is a link or a folder.

  • supplement_error_write: CITATION.cff or .zenodo.json cannot be read or written, or one of them does not exist and the site folder cannot be written.

  • supplement_error_release_write: a write of _supplement.yml, CITATION.cff, or .zenodo.json stopped, and the files that changed got their old text back, and each file that the release made was removed. If a file cannot be put back, the message names it. The error of the step is the parent of this error.

See also

check_supplement() for the checks, and write_citation() and write_zenodo() for the files that the release writes again.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In the folder of a rendered site in a git repository:
release_supplement("major")
} # }
